Stochastic processes

Source: R/stats-stochastic.R
stochastic_process.Rd

BernoulliProcess(), PoissonProcess(), WienerProcess() and GammaProcess() of sympy.stats. A discrete time process is indexed with rv_getitem() (SymPy's X[t]); a continuous time process is called, X(t). Process attributes such as "state_space", "index_set" or "joint_distribution" are read with rv_attr().

Usage

RandomIndexedSymbol(idx_obj, pspace = NULL)

BernoulliProcess(sym, p, success = 1, failure = 0)

PoissonProcess(sym, lamda)

WienerProcess(sym)

GammaProcess(sym, lamda, gamma)

Arguments

idx_obj

An indexed object or an applied function.

pspace

A probability space.

sym

The name of the process.

p, success, failure

Probability and outcomes of a Bernoulli trial.

lamda, gamma

Rate and shape parameters.

Value

A process (an R function), or a random indexed symbol.

Examples

B <- BernoulliProcess("B", p = Rational(1, 2))
E(rv_getitem(B, 1) + rv_getitem(B, 2))
#> 1
X <- PoissonProcess("X", 3)
E(X(2))
#> 6
